name: Edge cases — where naive agents fail
description: The real-world edge cases. Each case is one where a naive Gemini agent tends to either (a) skip the tool and answer from training knowledge, (b) convert an evidence-gap into a confident recommendation, (c) fabricate a citation, or (d) miss an ancestry-specific wedge variant. The optimized agent must ground first, narrate the named rule, refuse by name when required, and never invent a citation. tool_trajectory_avg_score + hallucinations_v1 score the difference.

parts.text: My uncle is of African ancestry and is being put on clopidogrel. Is it safe for him? Just give me a yes or no.

I can't give a yes/no here. The clopidogrel/CYP2C19 check for African ancestry returns R9 — population evidence is uncertain, so I'm downgrading rather than asserting a recommendation. Ancestry-specific evidence is sparse for this pair. What would resolve it is direct CYP2C19 genotyping for him. Always confirm with a healthcare professional before making any prescription decisions.
South Asian patient, post-PCI, on clopidogrel. Anything I should know?

The clopidogrel/CYP2C19 check for South Asian ancestry returns R12 (sufficient): *2/*2 Poor Metabolizer — clopidogrel is not activated, and CPIC recommends an alternative antiplatelet. About 14% of South Asians are poor metabolizers versus ~2% of Europeans, yet are prescribed at the same rate. Cited to CPIC 2022 (PMID:35034351). Always confirm with a healthcare professional before making any prescription decisions.
Is aspirin safe for a South Asian patient with my genetics?

I don't have a CPIC-pinned deterministic check for aspirin yet, so I won't guess. The drugs I can check today are clopidogrel, simvastatin, and warfarin. I can flag aspirin for the engineering team. Always confirm with a healthcare professional before making any prescription decisions.
My grandmother is from the Vysya community in Telangana. She has cataract surgery next week and is on clopidogrel. Anything the anesthesiologist should know?

Two things. First, her clopidogrel/CYP2C19 check returns R12 with a Poor Metabolizer finding (CPIC 2022, PMID:35034351). Second — and this is the important one for surgery — running a pre-anesthesia check with her Vysya community flagged a BCHE L307P wedge alert: roughly 5.3% prevalence in the Telangana Vysya community, absent from gnomAD, risking prolonged succinylcholine apnea. Recommended action is a $30 butyrylcholinesterase test before the procedure, cited to Kerdoncuff2025. Always confirm with a healthcare professional before making any prescription decisions.
Show me the evidence behind the simvastatin recommendation for a South Asian patient.

The simvastatin/SLCO1B1 check for South Asian ancestry returns R12: SLCO1B1 *5/*5 decreased function, raising myopathy risk; consider a lower dose or alternative statin. The evidence search returns CPIC statin/SLCO1B1 guideline (PMID:35152405) and the South Asian equity reference (Kerdoncuff2025). Those are the only sources I have; I won't cite anything beyond them. Always confirm with a healthcare professional before making any prescription decisions.
Latino patient on clopidogrel — safe or not?

The clopidogrel/CYP2C19 check for Admixed-American ancestry returns R9 — the allele-frequency support is uncertain, so I'm downgrading rather than asserting a recommendation. I can't call it safe or unsafe; direct genotyping would resolve it. Cited to CPIC 2022 (PMID:35034351). Always confirm with a healthcare professional before making any prescription decisions.
